transcript.text: Can you describe your role and key responsibilities as an Accounts Executive at the logistics firm?

I worked for a year as an accounts executive at a logistics firm in Jaipur. I processed about 300 vendor invoices a month, and cut the invoice backlog from six weeks to two. After that I took a year off to look after a family member. It was my choice and I don't regret it. In that time I did an online course on financial modelling to stay current. I now want an MBA to move from processing accounts to making financial decisions.
What specific actions did you take to reduce the invoice backlog from 6 weeks to 2 weeks?
transcript.anchor_quote: cut the invoice backlog from six weeks to two

transcript.text: The backlog fell because I grouped invoices by vendor and cleared the oldest vendors first. I also asked the warehouse to send delivery proof on the same day, which stopped many queries. I did that in my second quarter.
How did you measure the impact of these actions on your workflow and the overall finance team?
transcript.anchor_quote: I grouped invoices by vendor and cleared the oldest vendors first

transcript.text: The break gave me many life lessons. I learned patience, resilience and time management, and I think it made me a more well-rounded person and ready for all challenges.
You mentioned the break taught you patience, resilience, and time management. Can you give an example from your caregiving experience where these qualities helped you handle a difficult situation?
transcript.anchor_quote: I learned patience, resilience and time management

transcript.text: I would like to end the session here, please. I need to attend to something at home now. Could I see the feedback?

feedback.summary: The candidate effectively summarized their role and impact as an Accounts Executive, showing initiative in backlog reduction and continuous learning via financial modeling courses. They reflected positively on personal growth during their caregiving break and expressed clear motivation for pursuing an MBA to shift toward financial decision-making. However, depth on measuring impact and concrete examples from their caregiving experience were limited due to session ending early.
